## 2. Where the common definition comes from

Concept `tool-request-identity-and-arguments`: *Which tool was requested, under which native call id, by which response, with exactly which arguments?* Each foundation below was inspected for how it names a tool request; the decision says how Journal's definition relates to it (`journal-capture-tck/src/test/resources/ocsf/mapping-catalog/mapping-catalog.json`).

| Foundation | Its representation | Decision | Difference Journal keeps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spring_ai.release` | `AssistantMessage.ToolCall(id, type, name, arguments)` | adapt | Arguments are re-serialized to a string (Anthropic input converted via a JSON visitor), so native object form and lexical detail are not kept. |
| `spring_ai.development` | `ToolCallPart(toolCall=ToolCall(id, type, name, arguments), payload, attributes)` | adapt | String arguments; a provider index is local merge evidence, not a call id. |
| `acp.v1` | `tool_call.toolCallId, name, title, rawInput` | adapt | No link to the model response that requested it; rawInput is agent-reported, not necessarily the exact model arguments. |
| `otel_genai.semconv` | `ToolCallRequestPart{id,name,arguments}; execute_tool span gen_ai.tool.name, gen_ai.tool.call.id, gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` | adapt | Deserialization loses argument spelling; the requesting response is linked only by span context or ids. |
| `openinference.semconv` | `message.tool_calls.K.tool_call.{id,function.name,function.arguments}` | adapt | Arguments kept as a JSON string, close to the native text; requests are flattened attributes, not records. |
| `weave.agents_schema` | `execute_tool row: AgentSpanSchema.tool_call_id, tool_name, tool_call_arguments; tool_call part in the chat row` | adapt | Exact argument spelling is not preserved; pairing to the request is a join on id. |

Concept decision: **adapt**. Native call id, exact tool name and structured arguments; foundations carry arguments as a JSON string.

## 4. The reviewed meaning and the rule that executes it

The package declares its compatibility selection before any record is interpreted: entry `codex-cli/exec-json-stream/0.160.1`, status `tested`. Claims that cite this example as normative:

| Claim | Revision | Approval | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `codex.exec-stream.stream-local-identity` | r3 | proposed | Every item.id on Codex CLI exec --json is minted by the exec processor for its own stream (item_N); the app-server item id is dropped (a web search's second id aside). It is unique only within that source artifact of one Journal invocation (journal.run_uid, journal.invocation_index, source_ref.artifact): an equal item_0 in another invocation is another item. Journal uses it as tool_call_uid, operation uid and, on agent-message and reasoning content items, item_uid, each with identity_basis_id 2 Stream-local item identifier. It is never the model-facing call id or the provider's response id, which this route does not report: no response_uid is written, and one content item is not one model invocation. |
| `codex.exec-stream.mcp-tool-call` | r3 | proposed | A Codex CLI exec --json mcp_tool_call item.started reports a started invocation (tool_call activity 4 Started), not the model's original request: no model response owner, model call id or permission approval follows from it. tool_name = item.tool, tool_namespace = item.server, tool_family = mcp_tool_call, arguments = item.arguments exactly, reported_state = item.status. Its item.completed is the result of the same stream-local id: tool_result.data = item.result.content exactly (JSON null when the result has no content), structured_result = item.result.structured_content when not null, and the reported completed or failed status is the outcome (status_id 1 or 2, error_reported false or true; an MCP isError arrives as failed). An item observed only at completion has only its result. The kind is 99 Other unless a reviewed binding of the exact server and tool exists (none does): a name such as exec, Read or web_search never inherits a built-in kind. item.error and result._meta stay in the retained record. |

The mapping contract the package carries (declared in `events.jsonl` itself) names the rule each saved event executed:

| Rule | Native selector | Saved as | Contract text |
|---|---|---|---|
| `codex.stream.mcp_tool_call->tool_call.requested` | `{"type":"item.started","item.type":"mcp_tool_call"}` | 4 Started; tool_call_uid = item.id (identity_basis 2 stream-local) | tool_name = item.tool, tool_namespace = item.server, tool_family = mcp_tool_call, arguments = item.arguments exactly, reported_state = item.status; kind by codex.stream.mcp_namespace_kind.v1 (no binding: 99 other); a started invocation, not the model request: no response owner, model call id or permission decision follows |
| `codex.stream.mcp_tool_call->tool_call.result` | `{"type":"item.completed","item.type":"mcp_tool_call"}` | 2 Result observed; tool_call_uid = item.id (identity_basis 2 stream-local) | tool_result.data = item.result.content (null when result has none), structured_result = item.result.structured_content when not null, error_reported = item.status failed; status_id 1/2 from item.status (Reported); item.error stays in data; tool_name, tool_namespace and tool_family as on the start |

## 7. Misleading interpretations and what catches them

Each reviewed counterexample is applied to a copy of the saved package, and the oracle is run again. The rows list every check that is no longer VERIFIED.

### `model-facing-call-id`

item_1 is minted by the exec processor; claiming it is the model's call id would let a consumer join it with a native session's call ids, which it cannot match.

Edit: on the saved `tool_call` event for record 4 (activity 4), set `/identity_basis_id` = `1`.

| Check | Outcome | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `request.values` on `main/stream.jsonl` | DEFECTIVE | 4:item_1 identity_basis_id 1 != 2 |

### `server-folded-into-name`

The source reports server and tool separately; Journal never composes a tool name.

Edit: on the saved `tool_call` event for record 4 (activity 4), set `/tool_name` = `"fnd1/echo_record"`.

| Check | Outcome | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `request.values` on `main/stream.jsonl` | DEFECTIVE | 4:item_1 tool_name fnd1/echo_record != echo_record |

### `failed-as-success`

The item reports status failed; a result with content is not a success.

Edit: on the saved `tool_call` event for record 7 (activity 2), set `/status_id` = `1`.

| Check | Outcome | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `result.values` on `main/stream.jsonl` | DEFECTIVE | 7:item_2 status_id/status_basis_id 1/1 != 2/1 |

### `model-request-observed`

A started invocation is not the model's request; no response owner, model call id or permission decision follows from it.

Edit: a `tool_call` event with activity 1 added for record 4, carrying `/tool_call_uid` = `"item_1"`.

The added event is a copy of the record's existing `tool_call` event, so the checks on event order and whole-record retention also report the copy; the request population check reports the invented request itself.

| Check | Outcome | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `event.order` on `main` | DEFECTIVE | line 45 sequence 4 after 4 |
| `whole_record.coverage` on `main/stream.jsonl` | DEFECTIVE | record 4: 2 whole-record events |
| `population.requests` on `main/stream.jsonl` | DEFECTIVE | duplicated [4:item_1 x2] (expected 2, observed 3) |

Of 4 reviewed counterexamples, the oracle reports 4 as a changed check. The oracle's own mutation tests (for example `IdentityClassificationControlTest`) assert several of these outcomes in every build.
